| H123 | ~~**`offload-test-suite`'s `check-hlsl-feme-vk` target (first ever build+run this session) fails `Feature/DynamicResources/dyn-res-texture-sampler.test` with `"error: redefinition of symbol named 'SamplerDescriptorHeap.str'"`** at compute-pipeline creation~~: **CLOSED.** Root cause: DXC's own codegen for a shader that reads a bindless heap (`ResourceDescriptorHeap`/`SamplerDescriptorHeap`) through more than one distinct index expression can emit *two* separate `OpVariable`s for what is really the same heap binding (confirmed via `spirv-dis`: `%SamplerDescriptorHeap`/`%SamplerDescriptorHeap_0`, both `OpName`d `"SamplerDescriptorHeap"`, both `DescriptorSet 0`/`Binding 3`). MLIR's own SPIR-V deserializer does not de-duplicate these (it builds each `spirv.GlobalVariableOp` directly via `OpBuilder`, without re-verifying symbol-table uniqueness afterward), so `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`'s `prepareResourceVariables` saw two `spirv.GlobalVariableOp`s sharing one `sym_name`. Its own name-global uniquing loop (`for (unsigned Suffix = 0; Table.lookup(NameSymbol); ++Suffix) ...`) could never detect the collision: `Table` is a `mlir::SymbolTable` snapshotted once, before the loop starts creating any `<name>.str` LLVM globals, so it never reflects globals the loop itself has already created earlier in the same pass -- the second `SamplerDescriptorHeap.str` definition silently duplicated the first's name, surfacing only much later as an LLVM-level redefinition error at pipeline-creation time. | ~~H124e(a)~~ | ~~**`feme-cpu-wrap-entry`'s `matchLoopShape` cannot represent a loop whose structured-control-flow "latch" is a shared `Flow`-style merge block rather than a direct unconditional backedge to the header** -- **this session's own from-scratch IR-level dump/trace of both `InterlockedAdd.32.test` and the much simpler `WaveOps/GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync.test` (via `feme-opt --feme-convert-spirv-to-llvm` and manual CFG tracing through `feme-cpu-lower-wave`'s output, no code changes made) found the actual gap is narrower and more mechanical than the prior two-part "loop-carried-value spilling + nested-divergent-branch-in-loop-body" characterization below implied, and also corrects that characterization's own "two separate barriers per iteration" claim, which this session found was actually a *single* per-iteration barrier plus a wholly separate, unrelated barrier call *after* the loop entirely (in the suffix region), not two per iteration**. The real shape (confirmed identical in both repros, both produced by `feme::cpu::LoopLinearizer`): the header's `CondBrInst` tests the loop's trip count as normal, but its two successors are NOT "straight body chain ending in a direct backedge" plus "straight chain to the exit/suffix" as `matchLoopShape` requires -- instead, BOTH the header's own exit edge (via a critical-edge-split block, e.g. `.Flow_crit_edge`) and the body chain's own end (after doing one iteration's work, including its barrier) funnel into one shared merge block (`Flow`) that carries the loop's own live-out values as phis and re-decides, via its own `CondBrInst` on a phi that is a *compile-time-known distinct constant per predecessor edge* (e.g. `true` from the header-exit edge, `false` from the body edge), whether to continue (branch back to the header, via another critical-edge block e.g. `Flow._crit_edge`) or exit (continue into the suffix region). This `Flow` block's own branch is therefore not a genuine additional runtime test or divergent condition at all -- it is fully predictable per incoming edge -- but `matchLoopShape`'s current model has no notion of "latch and exit both routed through one shared merge block with a provably-constant-per-edge selector," and unconditionally rejects any block not covered by its `Prefix`/`Header`/`Body`/`Latch`/`Suffix` partition, which a shared `Flow` block never is. This shape is very likely present in *every* DXC/SPIR-V-Tools-structurized loop containing a barrier (a direct, mechanical consequence of SPIR-V's mandatory-merge-block structured-control-flow requirement, i.e. loop rotation with a guard), not a rare or exotic case -- meaning a `matchLoopShape` extension recognizing it would very likely close **most or all** of H124e's 9-case wrap-entry bucket at once, not just the 2 repros directly inspected this session. Concretely, the fix needs: (1) after the existing direct-backedge/`walkLinearChain` match attempt fails, try a second match: walk the body chain to a `PreLatch` block whose unconditional-branch target `M` is also the unconditional-branch target of a single-block critical-edge chain from the header's other successor; require `M`'s terminator to be a `CondBrInst` on a value provably constant-per-predecessor-edge for exactly these two edges; treat `PreLatch` as `Shape.Latch` and `M`'s constant-selected successor on the header-exit edge as the root of `ExitBlock`/`SuffixOrder` as today; and (2) correspondingly teach `buildWrapperForLoop`'s backedge-value threading that each `LoopInduction`'s per-iteration next-value is no longer `HeaderPhi->getIncomingValueForBlock(Shape.Latch)` directly, but one level of indirection further: the matching phi *at `M`* for the `PreLatch` edge (since the header's own phi now receives its value from `M` via the critical-edge block, not from `PreLatch` directly). This is a well-scoped, single-pattern CFG-recognition extension, not the previously-assumed two-part spilling-generalization-plus-nested-branch-support extension -- **not attempted this session** given the correctness risk of an under-tested CFG-transform change (a wrong fix here risks silently-incorrect wrapper output, not just a diagnosed failure) exceeding what could be thoroughly implemented, unit-tested, and CTS-regression-verified in one sitting; recommended as the concrete next-session starting point, ideally implemented and unit-tested first against the simpler `WaveOps/GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync.test` repro (one barrier, no extra inner branch) before attempting `InterlockedAdd.32.test`'s slightly more complex shape (which also has a genuine additional *uniform* inner branch inside the loop body, corresponding to the source's `if (I > 0 && ...)` short-circuit -- itself likely just an ordinary uniform `if` `matchBranchShape`/`DiamondFlattener` already know how to handle once nested inside a correctly-recognized loop body, not a separate new gap). Not yet re-confirmed against all 9 cases individually (only 2 of 9 traced this session), but the shape's universality argument above is strong grounds to expect it holds for the remaining 7 too **This session (H153) implemented exactly the two-piece design this row's own prior text proposed** (`JumpThreadingPass` insertion in `Pipeline.cpp` plus a `matchLoopShape` extension for the residual collapsed-single-block shape) and found it real but narrower than expected: `JumpThreadingPass` does NOT reliably eliminate the `Flow` merge block for every real DXC-produced case (confirmed via a real post-pass IR dump: `InterlockedExchange.32.test`'s own `Flow1._crit_edge` merge block survives fully intact, most likely because its loop body's own extra uniform branch makes the merge phi's incoming values non-constant on at least one edge) -- so this session's implementation only reaches the previously-designed `matchLoopShape` extension for the subset of cases where the merge block *does* thread away cleanly. The test's own golden `0` value for the all-`-INF` case only reproduces when the out-of-bounds-reading lanes and the valid-reading lanes share one subgroup/wave (subgroup size >= 8, true for typical desktop GPU subgroup sizes of 8/16/32/64), where an OOB read returning `0` (robustness-buffer zero-fill) pollutes the whole-wave `WaveActiveMax` reduction and drags every lane's result up to `0`. FeMe's own host-derived default wave size on this ARM/NEON host (`feme::cpu::hostDefaultWaveSize`, 4 here) is legitimately smaller: the `TID.x % 8` pattern happens to align exactly with 4-lane wave boundaries, so no wave ever mixes an OOB read with a valid one, and every wave (all-valid or all-OOB) reduces over uniform `-INF` values, correctly producing `-INF` -- not a miscompile, a genuine consequence of a smaller, still-spec-legal subgroup size exposing this test's own reliance on undefined behavior. Real CTS: `dEQP-VK.glsl.derivate.*.{fbo_float,texture.float}.*` (240 cases) go from every scalar-float subcase failing `vkQueueSubmit` to zero `queueSubmit` failures remaining -- 81/132 and 84/108 now pass outright, with the remaining 27+24 failing a real "Image comparison failed" for a distinct, not-yet-root-caused reason (a `dfdy`-heavy pattern, filed separately as H172 below), and 24/132 `NotSupported` for the unrelated, pre-existing `VK_SUBGROUP_FEATURE_QUAD_BIT` gate; (2) ~~`*.in_function.*` fails with `JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ spirv_var_13 ]`, suggesting a global-variable-linking gap when a derivative call (or possibly any GLSL builtin) is invoked from inside a helper function rather than `main` directly~~ -- **CLOSED.** Root cause: `canonicalizeSPIRVStage`'s stage-IO discovery/rewrite walk only ever covered its own entry-point `Function` argument, never a reachable, not-yet-inlined helper function's own instructions -- so a GLSL/glslang-sourced helper's direct `load`/`store` of a module-scope `Input`/`Output` global (a shape `dxc`'s own HLSL lowering never produces, since it always fully inlines a helper before this pipeline ever sees it) survived unconverted straight through `feme::cpu::InlineHelperFunctionsPass`'s later inlining, reaching the CPU JIT as a genuinely external, never-defined symbol. Confirmed as a real, deterministic (not flaky) 72/72 failure of the entire `in_function` bucket at the pre-fix baseline -- an earlier session's own claim that this bucket "passes 72/72"/"is rare/hard to reproduce" was itself an artifact of an environment bug (`export A=x B=$A` shell-expansion-order pitfall silently routing some test invocations at llvmpipe rather than FeMe; see agent_thoughts.md). Fix: `canonicalizeSPIRVStage` now walks every function transitively reachable from the entry via ordinary (not yet inlined) calls -- stopping at another entry point or a declaration -- for both the discovery pass and the actual load/store rewrite, constructing a `ShadowValueMap` once per function in that set (needed since it places its own read-back shadow allocas in *its* function's entry block) rather than once for the entry alone. An earlier attempt at fixing this by reordering `InlineHelperFunctionsPass` to run before `CanonicalizeStagePass` in `feme::cpu::runPipeline` was abandoned: it caused severe, nondeterministic regressions (segfaults in JIT-compiled code) elsewhere in the same bucket, for reasons not fully understood, in favor of this more surgical, pass-internal fix. Real CTS: all 72 `dEQP-VK.glsl.derivate.*.in_function.*` cases go from fail to pass deterministically (verified against the real FeMe device, 3 repeated runs); `check-hlsl-feme-vk` unchanged (376 pass / 1 pre-existing `array_of_matrices.test` XPASS flake, no regressions); (3) ~~`*.private_store.*` scalar-float subcases fail via a bare "Image comparison failed"~~ -- **CLOSED for the scalar-float subcases.** Root-caused via `FEME_DUMP_IR=1`: SPIR-V `Private`-storage-class file-scope variables (and, identically, purely-local `alloca`s) written under *uniform* control flow with a per-lane-*divergent* value were never recognized by `SIMDizePass`'s `FunctionWidener::collectMaskedAllocas()`, which previously only flagged an alloca for real per-lane storage when reached via a `feme.cpu.masked.load/store` call -- something `LinearizePass` only ever emits inside genuinely divergent control flow. A plain, unconditional store of a divergent value (e.g. `intermediateStore = v_coord;` at the top of a shader) silently let every lane's store overwrite the same one scalar slot, so only the last lane's value survived, later broadcast to all lanes on read -- a full miscompile (matches the "entire framebuffer black" qpa symptom exactly), not a subtle math bug. Two-part fix in `SIMDize.cpp`: (a) `checkVectorDecompositionSupported` now accepts a `Derivative*`/`QuadRead` stage-op call as both a supported vector-typed producer (its own result) and consumer (a vector-typed value used as such a call's argument) -- deliberately *not* extended to other vector-capable `StageOpKind`s like a hypothetical vector `TaskPayloadLoad`, which would need genuine per-component address arithmetic; (b) `widenStageOp` decomposes a vector-typed call into `N` independent per-component wide stage-op calls (mirroring `widenVectorElementwise`'s existing decomposition pattern), safe because both derivative and quad-read semantics are genuinely component-wise independent (GLSL/HLSL define `dFdx`/`dFdy`/`fwidth` of a vector per-component, and a quad-read gathers the same source lane for every component). `WaveLoweringPass::lowerDerivative`/`lowerQuadRead` needed **no changes** -- they already generically expect any `WaveSize`-sized vector operand and have no notion of "components" at all, so they lower each of the `N` decomposed calls exactly as they would any naturally-scalar one. Reloading at the top of the use's own barrier region instead makes such a use correct, so the guard relaxes to: the use precedes the recurrence, *or* shares its barrier region (no group-sync barrier between them), *or* lives in the loop's post-loop suffix chain (where the slot holds exactly the value the header phi would carry on the exiting edge). This alone closed `InterlockedExchange.32.test`. (b) *Non-barrier chain boundaries.* A wave body's prefix, loop and suffix chains are outlined into *separate* functions, so a chain boundary is a region boundary even with no barrier on it; `spillValuesLiveAcrossBarriers` only knew about barriers and left every prefix-defined, loop-used value as a cross-function reference (`Referring to an instruction in another function!`). It now takes the boundaries as indices, with the two chain boundaries added alongside the barriers. (c) *Stranded scalar recurrences.* When H159(a) outlines the latch, a genuinely uniform scalar recurrence living in it (typically the trip counter, `%N = add i32 %phi, 1`) becomes unusable -- it is inside a per-wave region, yet the header reads it, so it cannot be wave-persistent either. That only holds for its no-barrier and straight-line-barrier (`splitAtGroupSyncBarriers`) paths, both of which reuse the original `Function`'s own identity for their final outlined region -- `buildWrapperForLoop`/`buildWrapperForBranch` (the `LoopShape`/`BranchShape` paths) always call `WaveBody->eraseFromParent()` unconditionally once wrapped, since none of their own outlined prefix/body/suffix regions are obligated to keep the original name. `Mod.getFunction(EntryName)` therefore returns null for *every* successfully-wrapped loop/branch shape, producing a spurious "entry point 'main' did not survive the CPU pipeline" error regardless of whether `EntryWrapperPass` actually succeeded -- this had been silently masking every real fix to the H124e/H124e(a)/H155 wrap-entry bucket at the runtime layer, one level above where all that work was actually happening.~~ **Fixed**: `GroupSize` is now read from the entry point's own `hlsl.numthreads` function attribute *before* the pipeline runs (`getDeclaredGroupSize(**Entry)`), exactly mirroring how `SideEffectFlags`/`Signature` are already computed pre-pipeline just above it -- this attribute is stable and unaffected by anything the pipeline itself does. The post-pipeline survival check now instead verifies `Mod.getFunction(WrapperName)` (the actual JIT lookup target used just below it), not `EntryName`. New regression test `CompiledStageTest.LoopWithBarrierSurvivesCompiledStageCreation` compiles and *invokes* an end-to-end loop-with-barrier compute shader through the real `CompiledStage::create` path, verifying both `getGroupSize()` and correct output. | H150 | **`WaveOps/WaveActiveMax.test`'s `NegInfs` sub-case (split out of H147a once individually triaged): triaged this session, found to be *not* a fixable FeMe code bug, but a host-CPU-vector-width-dependent test artifact.** Reproduced standalone: actual output stays `[-inf, -inf, -inf, -inf]` (the input, unchanged) against an expected `[0, 0, 0, 0]`. Root-caused: the test dispatches 32 threads with `numthreads(32,1,1)` and no explicit wave-size requirement, so `feme::cpu::resolveWaveSize`'s host-derived default (`max(4, HostVectorBits / 32)`) picks the actual subgroup size -- on this session's ARM64/NEON host (128-bit vectors), that resolves to the documented `MinWaveSize` floor of 4. `NegInfs[TID.x % 8]` reads/writes indices 0-7 from a 4-element buffer (`Data: [-inf, -inf, -inf, -inf]`), so half the accesses (indices 4-7) are out-of-bounds; with `robustBufferAccess`, an out-of-bounds *read* returns 0. The test's own expected `0` result only arises if a *single* `WaveActiveMax` reduction's active lane set spans **both** an in-bounds index (real `-inf`) and an out-of-bounds index (robust-zero `0`) -- i.e. only if the actual subgroup size is >= 8, mixing the two together (`max(-inf, 0) = 0`, broadcast to every lane in that reduction). At this host's actual wave size of 4, every subgroup's 4 lanes all read the *same* index bucket (all in-bounds or all out-of-bounds), so no such mixing ever happens and the reduction correctly stays `-inf` (its own SPIR-V-defined identity) -- matching this session's observed actual output exactly. `Nans`/`Infs`/`Mix` (the other 3 buffers in the same test) already pass, confirmed unaffected (their expected values are invariant to this mixing either way: `inf`/`nan`-dominated reductions produce the same result regardless of whether a `0` from an OOB read joins the mix). **Not a FeMe correctness bug** -- `feme::cpu::resolveWaveSize`'s host-derived default is itself a documented, deliberate design choice (`feme/docs/FeMeCPUDesign.md`'s "Wave Size Selection"), and this test's own expectation is inherently tied to whatever subgroup size >= 8 the reference implementation that authored it used; nothing to fix in FeMe itself, though the test itself is not portable to every legal host wave size FeMe's own design permits. If ever revisited: could confirm by re-running with a wave size >= 8 forced via `--wave-size` (not currently plumbed through the Vulkan ICD's own device-property query path, which hardcodes `UserWaveSize=std::nullopt` -- see `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp`) | H147a | N/A -- host-dependent test artifact, not a FeMe bug | P4 |

| ~~H135~~ | ~~**`layOutStructIfOffsetsMatch` builds a non-`packed` `!llvm.struct`, silently corrupting every array of an offset-decorated struct whose true size undershoots its largest member's ABI alignment** (found while investigating a reported `check-hlsl-feme-vk` run-to-run flakiness, which itself turned out to be a false alarm caused by two missing environment variables in one particular invocation, not a real nondeterminism -- but the investigation's own from-scratch re-run of the full suite surfaced this genuinely new bug instead): an ordinary (non-`packed`) `!llvm.struct` always rounds its own total size up to its largest member's ABI alignment via *implicit* trailing padding invisible to any explicit member list (e.g. `{vector<2xf32>, f32}`, true size 12, silently becomes size 16 due to the vector's 8-byte alignment) -- harmless for a single, standalone struct value, but fatal for `!llvm.array<N x StructTy>` (which has no independent stride field, always exactly `sizeof(StructTy)` per element): any `RWStructuredBuffer<B>`-shaped SSBO/UBO array of a struct `B` with this size/alignment mismatch got corrupted spacing between elements~~ -- **fixed, in three steps this session after two regressions were caught by this same session's own validation runs**: (1) build the final `LLVMStructType::getLiteral` call with `isPacked=true` for the offset-decorated branch, and changed the existing gap-insertion condition from `NaturalCursor < DeclaredOffset` to `Cursor < DeclaredOffset` so a *purely alignment-driven* gap (one a non-packed struct would have supplied silently) is now always materialized as an explicit `[N x i8]` member too, since packing removes that implicit padding entirely; (2) this first correction broke `CompositeConstructOp`'s `convertStruct` pattern, which had assumed the SPIR-V struct's declared member count always equals the LLVM struct's physical field count -- true before this fix (gaps were rare, handled by other retry tiers with known index-remap machinery) but now false whenever *any* gap gets materialized -- fixed by mapping each declared member index to its physical index via the existing `getStructMemberPhysicalIndex` helper, previously only used by access-chain patterns; (3) this session's own `dEQP-VK.ssbo.*` full-sweep validation (12,225 cases) then caught a second, more subtle regression: 36 `dEQP-VK.ssbo.layout.multi_nested_struct.*`/`unsized_nested_struct_array.*` cases newly failed, root-caused to `mlir::DataLayout::getTypeABIAlignment` returning `1` for *any* packed LLVM struct (a correct reflection of LLVM's own packed-struct semantics) -- which broke the "is this gap natural" alignment check for an *outer* struct containing a (now-always-packed) offset-decorated nested struct member: the nested struct's true natural alignment (what it would have had, non-packed) collapsed to 1, making every gap before/after it look like a false "interior" gap needing `AllowInteriorPad` (never set on this function's first, ordinary attempt), forcing the whole struct through several failing retry tiers and eventually the unrelated tight-vector-substitution tier, which does not correctly handle a matrix column in this doubly-nested shape. #### 1.9.8 Ray tracing (J-series)

Ray tracing is not part of the Vulkan 1.4 core floor: `VK_KHR_ray_query`,
`VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline` and `VK_KHR_acceleration_structure` are
optional extensions, and a 1.4 conformance submission is valid without any
of them. They are in scope anyway, per
[FeMeVulkanDesign.md](FeMeVulkanDesign.md)'s "Conformance Target": the CTS's
ray-tracing groups are the only conformance-grade tests that exist for the
traversal and continuation machinery
[FeMeGraphicsDesign.md](FeMeGraphicsDesign.md)'s G7/G8 design, and both
report zero failures today only because nothing is advertised.

Two properties make this series different from every other one in §1.9,
and both change how it should be distributed:

- **It is a dependency chain, not a set of independent rows.** Nothing can
  be advertised until J1-J4 all land, because the extension set's own
  `requires` graph forbids advertising a member without its prerequisites
  (see FeMeVulkanDesign.md's "Mesh shading and ray tracing exposure").
- **Most of the work is in `feme::graphics`/a new `feme::raytracing`, not
  in `lib/Vulkan`.** The Vulkan rows below are the API mapping; G7/G8 are
  the engine. Direct3D's DXR (FeMeWARPDesign.md's W6) reuses the same
  engine, which is why it is worth building once, carefully, rather than
  twice.

| # | Task | Depends on | Files | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | **Buffer device address** (`bufferDeviceAddress`, core since 1.2, currently `VK_FALSE` in the aggregate `VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features` case). Every acceleration-structure build input and shader binding table is addressed by `VkDeviceAddress`, so this is the true first row: `vkGetBufferDeviceAddress`, a device-address space over this ICD's own allocations, and the bounds model that turns an attacker-supplied address back into a checked allocation + offset. Also unblocks `VK_KHR_buffer_device_address`'s own CTS coverage independently of ray tracing | none | `feme/lib/Vulkan/{Memory,Buffer}.{h,cpp}`, `EntryPoints.cpp` | P0 |

Not ray tracing itself, but the `dEQP-VK.ray_tracing_pipeline` corpus leans on it heavily, and the shader-side non-uniform indexing is a `feme::cpu` question (a divergent descriptor index through the existing heap model) rather than an API one | §1.2, R26 | `feme/lib/Vulkan/Descriptor.{h,cpp}`, `feme/lib/Target/CPU` | P1 |

This ICD already owns a worker pool (roadmap R21), so a truthful implementation is either a real deferral onto it or an honest "everything completes immediately"; both are legal, and the second is a good first row for a new contributor | none | new `feme/lib/Vulkan/DeferredOperation.{h,cpp}` | P1 |

#### 1.9.9 What "full Vulkan 1.4 conformance" is done against

A single, checkable definition, so that "are we conformant yet" never
becomes a matter of opinion. All five must hold simultaneously:

1. **Zero `Fail`** in the mandatory `deqp-vk` list for
   `VK_API_VERSION_1_4`, plus zero `Fail` in `dEQP-VK.ray_query` and
   `dEQP-VK.ray_tracing_pipeline` for the advertised ray-tracing set
   (§1.9.8's own criterion; not required for the submission itself).
2. **Zero crashed or truncated groups.** The current run has seven
   (headline table, VulkanCTSReport.md); a crashed group's totals are not
   a result at all.
3. **Every mandatory feature, limit, format and queue capability
   advertised and truthful** — §1.9.4 (E), §1.9.5 (F) and §1.9.7 (H)
   closed, cross-checked against
   [Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md](Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md) regenerated
   from the registry rather than from this tree's notes.
4. **A stock, unpatched CTS** (roadmap C9), on a build with assertions
   enabled.
5. **Reproduced by the continuous job** (C10/D4/G1-G2), not by a
   hand-run sweep, so that the claim survives the next commit.

Milestone V9 in [FeMeVulkanDesign.md](FeMeVulkanDesign.md) owns turning
this into an actual submission (driver ID, conformance version, submission
package).

#### 1.9.10 The 1.1/1.2 floor this ICD skipped (K-series)

§1.9.4 and §1.9.5 close 1.3 and 1.4. They assume the versions *below*
them are closed, because roadmap C6 closed the 1.2 floor — but C6 closed
it as a list of *feature bits and limits*, derived by hand, and never
checked which promoted *extensions* those bits belonged to. Regenerating
[Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md](Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md) over 1.0-1.4
rather than 1.3/1.4 is what surfaced the difference:

- **Zero of Vulkan 1.1's twelve feature bits are advertised**
  (`multiview`, `variablePointers`/`variablePointersStorageBuffer`, the
  four 16-bit storage bits, `samplerYcbcrConversion`,
  `shaderDrawParameters`, `protectedMemory`, and the two multiview stage
  bits). A 1.4 claim inherits all of them.
- **Seven of 1.2's 47 are**, so 40 remain — the whole descriptor-indexing
  cluster, 8-bit storage, `shaderFloat16`/`shaderInt8`, `scalarBlockLayout`,
  `bufferDeviceAddress`, the Vulkan memory model, `drawIndirectCount`,
  `samplerFilterMinmax`, `samplerMirrorClampToEdge`,
  `shaderOutputViewportIndex`/`shaderOutputLayer`, the int64 atomics.
- **Eleven core-promoted extensions are only partially implemented**, which
  neither inventory can express and which reads as a bare "no" in both:
  `VK_KHR_dedicated_allocation`, `VK_KHR_device_group`,
  `VK_KHR_get_memory_requirements2`,
  `VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2`, `VK_KHR_maintenance2`,
  `VK_KHR_multiview`, `VK_KHR_shader_draw_parameters`,
  `VK_EXT_sampler_filter_minmax`, `VK_KHR_sampler_mirror_clamp_to_edge`,
  `VK_KHR_separate_depth_stencil_layouts`, `VK_KHR_spirv_1_4`.

The distinction that orders this series: a promoted extension's *commands*
are mandatory even when its *feature* may be reported false. This ICD's
own rule already says so — FeMeVulkanDesign.md's "Initial Non-Goals": "An
advertised core version may report a feature as unsupported; it may not
omit a command." K1 is that rule applied; the rest are features.

being about versions two releases old.

### 1.10 Direct3D software adapter

Owned by [FeMeWARPDesign.md](FeMeWARPDesign.md). Nothing exists.

| Gap | Owner section | Priority |

| The integration boundary is undecided: whether a software/render-only adapter can be installed and enumerated through DXGI at all, versus an application-local compatibility runtime. Choosing wrong invalidates most object-layer work, so W0 is explicitly a throwaway-capable prototype and gates every Windows-facing line of code | "Replacement and Deployment Model", W0 | P0 |
| No Windows SDK/WDK/DDI version selection, signing, INF, CI or debugging story — and no Windows CI in this tree at all | W0 | P0 |
| Same in-process LLVM coexistence requirement as §1.9 (the adapter loads into processes that may already host DXC), plus an exported symbol set checked against the selected DDI contract | "Project and Binary Boundaries" | P0 |
| Serialized root signatures of both versions, descriptor heaps and tables | W2 | P1 |
| Device/queue/allocator/list/fence/heap/buffer/pipeline objects, device-removal propagation, indirect dispatch, copies, barriers, queries | W1–W2 | P1 |
| Textures, sampling, copy footprints, views, format matrix | W3 | P1 (blocked on G2) |
| Raster, output merge, tessellation/geometry, pipeline libraries, persistent cache, HLK | W4–W5 | P2 (blocked on G3–G5) |
| DXGI presentation, shared resources/fences, D3D11-on-12 evaluation | W6 | P2 |
| DXR (state objects, ray-tracing pipelines, shader tables, inline ray tracing at `D3D12_RAYTRACING_TIER_1_1`) and mesh/amplification shading, both now inside the declared scope rather than "evaluate later" | W6 | P2 (blocked on G6–G8, and on §1.9.8 proving the shared engine against the Vulkan CTS first) |
| No conformance measurement of any kind is possible in this tree: the HLK is Windows-only and there is no Windows CI, so the shared graphics/ray-tracing core's conformance evidence comes from the Vulkan side until W0 solves that | W7 | P1 |

Its portable half (command execution, resource layout, software graphics) is
required to stay unit-testable on non-Windows hosts, which is what makes W1–W5
partially reviewable in this tree at all; only `lib/Direct3D/Windows` is
genuinely Windows-only.

#### 1.10.1 The equivalent conformance scope

[FeMeWARPDesign.md](FeMeWARPDesign.md)'s "Conformance Target" now states the
Direct3D counterpart of §1.9.9's definition: feature level 12_2 in full
(DXR 1.1, mesh shaders, sampler feedback, variable-rate shading, binding
tier 3), measured by the HLK Direct3D 12 suites and this project's own
portable execution tests, with the same "advertise only what passes" rule.
Two scheduling facts follow, and both are the reason this stays a §1.10
note rather than its own E/F/H/J-style series:

- **The work is mostly already scheduled, under other names.** Everything
  the Direct3D target needs from the shared core is a G-row (G2–G8) or,
  transitively, a §1.9.7/§1.9.8 row that drives one. Adding a parallel
  Direct3D row per capability would double-track the same engine work; what
  is genuinely Direct3D-specific stays in W0–W7.
- **It is deliberately behind Vulkan, not beside it.** The Vulkan CTS runs
  on this project's hosts today and the HLK does not, so the shared core
  reaches conformance quality through §1.9 first. "Eventually equivalent"
  is a scope statement, not a schedule one — and W7 is the milestone that
  makes it checkable rather than aspirational.

The one thing this section *does* add is an obligation on §1.9.7/§1.9.8
rows: a fix landed in `feme::graphics`/`feme::raytracing` for a Vulkan CTS
failure must not be written as if Vulkan were its only consumer, because
W4–W7 will re-run the same code under Direct3D semantics. Where the two
APIs genuinely differ (raster rules, coordinate origins, precision
requirements), the difference belongs in the API runtime, per
FeMeGraphicsDesign.md's "Architectural Boundary" — recording which of the
two it is, in the fix itself, is what keeps the Direct3D side from
rediscovering it as a bug.

### 1.11 HLSL conformance via offload-test-suite

Owned by no single design document yet (a real gap-inventory row, not a
design-document deviation): `llvm/offload-test-suite`'s `beanz/feme` branch
wires up a `check-hlsl-feme-vk` lit target running that suite's real HLSL
(`dxc`-compiled) test corpus against this project's own Vulkan ICD, a
substantially different (and, for many shapes, entirely new) source of
SPIR-V than every §1.9 row's own `deqp-vk`-derived GLSL coverage. A first
full run (612 discovered tests) found 268 real failures; this section
tracks the buckets a per-failure-signature triage of that run's own full
verbose log found, one row per coherent root cause/cluster, following the
same "max one lowercase letter of nesting" convention every H/J/K row
above uses.

| Gap | Owner section | Priority |

An HLSL/DXIL-sourced module never exercises this gap because `dxc` always fully inlines every user-defined function into its entry point long before this pipeline ever sees it; only a GLSL/glslang-compiled module (where a non-trivial helper routinely survives as a real, separate `OpFunction`/`OpFunctionCall` pair) reaches this pipeline with more than one non-declaration function in the first place -- which is why this bug affects the *entire* `ComputeBackend` harness (every case calls its own `interpolate()`-shaped helper) regardless of filter mode, mipmapping, or explicit-Grad-ness, matching every one of this session's own bisection results. New `feme::cpu::InlineHelperFunctionsPass` (`InlineHelperFunctions.h`/`.cpp`) closes this: it marks every non-entry-point function `alwaysinline`+`internal` and runs `llvm::AlwaysInlinerPass` followed by `llvm::GlobalDCEPass`, restoring the "exactly one non-declaration function per shader stage" invariant every later pass already assumed, as the new first step of the CPU pipeline (before even `SPIRVBuiltinFoldingPass` -- see `feme/lib/Target/CPU/Pipeline.cpp`). A no-op (skipped outright) for the common HLSL/DXIL-sourced-module case. 4 new unit tests (`InlineHelperFunctionsTest.cpp`): a single helper call, multiple call sites of the same helper, nested helper calls, and the already-fully-inlined no-op case. The real shape (`Feature/CBuffer/array-of-structs.test`/`dynamic-struct.test`'s own `uint x[2]; uint q;`) is `struct<S, (array<2 x i32, stride=16> [0], i32 [20])>`: real HLSL/Vulkan layout semantics require every array element *except the last* to occupy the full declared stride (so a dynamic index into `x[1]` still addresses correctly), but the array's own occupied footprint for a *subsequent* sibling member's own placement is only `(N-1)*Stride + NaturalSize(last element)` -- i.e. `q` is allowed to pack into the otherwise-unused trailing padding of `x`'s own last element. A single, homogeneous `LLVM::LLVMArrayType` cannot represent "N-1 stride-wide elements plus one natural-size element" at all (every element, including the last, must be the same width); representing it instead as a heterogeneous struct (`struct<(array<(N-1) x Padded>, Unpadded)>`) cannot support a *dynamic* (runtime-value) index selecting between the array portion and the final-element portion, since LLVM `getelementptr` struct-member selection requires a compile-time-constant index -- a materially harder problem than L13a's own append-only padding. Needs its own scoping pass to determine whether a dynamic index into such an array can be legalized at all without either (a) always widening the *last* element to the full stride too (over-allocating by `Stride - NaturalSize(last)` bytes, wasting space but preserving a uniform array and requiring no representation change), or (b) a real heterogeneous-with-dynamic-index scheme this codebase does not have a precedent for anywhere yet~~ (done: generalized `convertArrayTypeIgnoringDecorations` so a non-struct array element undershooting its declared stride substitutes a uniform `Stride`-sized opaque byte-array stand-in for every element (mirroring `getTightVectorArrayType`'s identical opaque-pointer-safe reasoning) instead of returning `nullptr` -- this alone handles the general case, including a genuinely *dynamic* SPIR-V index, resolving option (a)'s real scope (uniform widening's own memory-correctness limitation -- not merely "wasted space" -- is that it only works when no sibling's own declared offset conflicts with the widened footprint). Added a new, narrower helper, `convertUndersizedScalarArrayMemberIgnoringDecorations`, for the sibling-conflicting case: a literal heterogeneous LLVM struct with one member per array element (the `Stride`-sized stand-in for every element except the last, which keeps its own real, unpadded type), reproducing the sibling's true declared offset -- this relies on `LLVM::GEPOp`'s own `destructureIndices` auto-detecting a compile-time-constant SPIR-V index when navigating a literal struct type (confirmed via `LLVMDialect.cpp`), so it is scoped to constant-index accesses only (true of every real `dxc`-emitted HLSL array index in the affected tests); a genuinely dynamic index into this specific sibling-conflicting shape remains unsupported, a real residual limitation matching option (b)'s own "no precedent" framing, not merely a documentation gap. | ~~L124(u)~~ | ~~**`ssbo.*`'s sole remaining `Fail`** (of 12,225 total, down from 4 at L124(t)'s start), re-scoped from L124(t) above: `dEQP-VK.ssbo.layout.random.nested_structs_instance_arrays.8` ("Result comparison and counter values are incorrect"). A considerably more complex shader than any other L124 repro so far -- three buffer blocks (`BlockB`/`BlockC`/`BlockD`), six distinct nested struct types (`sA`-`sF`), and several distinct matrix shapes~~ **Root-caused and fixed this session**: `getStructMemberPhysicalIndex`'s "redo" of a nested struct's own physical layout (used by `remapNestedStructMemberIndices` to translate a declared struct-member index into its real physical index) converts the nested struct **standalone**, as if it were top-level. For `sB` (itself nested inside `sD`, itself `BlockC.f`'s own struct member), that standalone conversion trivially succeeds at the "natural" (tier 1) retry -- a bare `vec3` member's generic/rounded LLVM size (16 bytes) happens to exactly reach the next member's declared offset in isolation. But `sB` embedded for real inside `sD` uses a **different, correct** physical layout: `sD`'s own natural-tier conversion fails (its own `i32` member right after `sB` can't be reached without a gap), forcing a retry at the `VectorOnly` tier, whose per-member substitution loop unconditionally calls `getTightNestedStructType` on any nested-struct member -- always force-tightening every interior vector/matrix member of that nested struct regardless of whether the nested struct would need tightening in isolation. This means whether a nested struct's own body gets tightened is a property of **which retry tier its enclosing struct actually needed**, not an intrinsic property of the nested struct type itself -- exactly the class of bug this whole roadmap item (L124) keeps re-encountering in new shapes, just now confirmed at the struct-member-index level rather than the matrix-widening level. Fixed by a new `getStructMemberPhysicalIndexInRealType`, which reads the declared-to-physical index mapping directly off the already-known-correct real LLVM type used by the immediate enclosing struct's own conversion (walking its body in declared-offset order), rather than re-deriving the nested struct's layout independently; `remapNestedStructMemberIndices` now tracks this real type across nested-struct levels (reset to null when the walk passes through an array level, conservatively preserving prior behavior there). | ~~L124(m)~~ | ~~**`2_level_array`/`3_level_array`/`3_level_unsized_array`'s own residual 12 `Fail`s each (36 total), left after L124(f)'s column-select fix**: not yet individually re-triaged -- L124(f)'s fix closed these families' column-select cases but something else in the same families still fails (possibly a scalar-element variant, or a whole-access edge case L124(i)/(j) didn't cover for 3-level nesting specifically); needs its own `FEME_DUMP_IR=1` trace on one repro from each family before assuming a shared root cause with L124(k)/(l)~~ **Done**: root-caused to a silent miscompile (wrong numeric result, not a legalization failure) of a `RowMajor`/`MatrixStride`-decorated *non-square* matrix (e.g. `mat4x3`) reached through 2+ levels of array nesting. `convertArrayTypeIgnoringDecorations` correctly declines when a non-square matrix's natural (vector-padded) LLVM size exceeds the declared `ArrayStride`, but that decline falls through to MLIR upstream's own `spirv::ArrayType` conversion, which validates the stride against a *different* natural-size calculation for matrices (tightly-packed scalar count, not vector-padded) -- since that check can still pass even when the two notions of "natural size" disagree, upstream silently built the array around the wrong (too-large) matrix conversion instead of erroring out. This manifested in two call sites in `rewriteBlockAccess`: the initial `ElementType` computation (whole-matrix access, 2+ array levels) and the `NeedsDeepNestingPeel` loop's per-iteration `PeeledElementType` computation (partial/column-select access, 3+ array levels). Fixed both via a new shared helper, `substituteArrayOfMatrixElementType`, which substitutes the correct physical matrix type (via the pre-existing `getPhysicalMatrixMemberType`/`wrapPhysicalMatrixInArrays`) whenever the naive conversion isn't representable. This fix is purely a type-spelling change for square matrices (where the bug was invisible, since natural and physical sizes coincide) -- required updating one pre-existing test's CHECK line, with no behavioral change (same GEP byte size/stride, same actual load/store types). New `spirv-to-llvm-matrix-rowmajor-nonsquare-nested-array-block.mlir` regression test (whole-access fix); the partial-access (`NeedsDeepNestingPeel`) fix is covered by the real CTS sweep itself (`3_level_array`/`3_level_unsized_array`'s own `_store_cols` cases), since a synthetic unit-test repro for that specific 3-level shape could not be legalized for unrelated reasons and was not pursued further given the CTS evidence. Root-caused via `--deqp-log-decompiled-spirv=enable`: `types.bool`'s shader declares several *bare scalar* `i1` `Workgroup` globals, each loaded directly with no `AccessChain` at all; `composites.2`'s shader has one `Workgroup` struct global mixing a plain `i1` member with `bvec2`/`bvec3`/`bvec4` members, accessed via ordinary `AccessChain`s. Both were rejected outright by `WorkgroupGlobalVariablePattern`'s own `containsAddressableBool` guard (`feme/lib/Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM/SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`), which assumed *any* `i1` inside a `Workgroup` aggregate is unaddressable by `getelementptr` -- confirmed via a direct `mlir-translate -mlir-to-llvmir` + `opt -passes=verify` repro that this assumption is simply wrong for every shape FeMe's own conversion produces: a struct member's own `getelementptr` index is always a fixed byte offset (never a runtime multiply-by-element-size the way array/vector indexing is), and LLVM's data layout already reserves a full byte for an `i1` array element's own stride. The one shape that genuinely can't use `getelementptr` -- indexing a single lane out of a `bool` *vector* -- was never even covered by this guard's own struct/array-only recursion in the first place, and is already handled correctly by the pre-existing `BoolVectorLaneAccessChainPattern`/`BoolVectorLaneLoadPattern`/`BoolVectorLaneStorePattern` (full-vector load/store plus `extractelement`/`insertelement`). Fixed by removing the guard entirely. Below that, `int_spv_resource_gather` (`llvm/include/llvm/IR/IntrinsicsSPIRV.td`) has a single, fixed `(image, sampler, coord, component, offset)` shape with room for exactly one flat offset vector, and `SPIRVInstructionSelector::selectGatherIntrinsic` (`llvm/lib/Target/SPIRV/SPIRVInstructionSelector.cpp`) only ever emits the `ConstOffset`/`Offset` (singular) SPIR-V image operand bits from that one offset register -- confirmed via `grep -rn "ConstOffsets"` across the whole LLVM SPIR-V backend and MLIR SPIR-V dialect: the *bit* exists (`SPIRVSymbolicOperands.td`'s `ConstOffsets : ImageOperandOperand<0x20, [ImageGatherExtended]>`, `SPIRVBase.td`'s `SPIRV_IO_ConstOffsets`), but **zero code anywhere consumes it for lowering purposes** -- the only other reference is `ImageOps.cpp`'s own `verifyImageOperands` TODO-assert (the same one L35(a) worked around for `feme-translate --import-spirv` specifically; irrelevant here since the real runtime path skips full verification). This means implementing `ConstOffsets` support requires new plumbing at every layer, not just a missing feme-side switch case, and does not fit safely in one small change -- split into two new, independently-completable rows below (L125(m)/L125(n)) rather than attempted as one unscoped blob. Root cause: `CommandBuffer.cpp`'s `decodeASTCImageForSampling`/`decodeBCImageForSampling`/`decodeETC2ImageForSampling` (the host-side compressed-block-to-RGBA8/target-format decode bridge feeding the CPU runtime's own sampling path, since `FeMeRuntimeCPU.c` has no block-compressed case of its own) were **hardcoded to array layer 0 / depth slice 0 only** by original design (roadmap E23/H8j/H8n's own explicit scope), with `materializeImageDescriptor` early-returning an all-zero descriptor for any nonzero base layer or `LayerCount != 1` range rather than silently decoding the wrong layer. (1) **The dominant bug (~810 of 814)**: `VkSamplerCreateInfo::unnormalizedCoordinates` was never read anywhere in the codebase (confirmed via a zero-hit grep) -- every CPU-runtime sampling function unconditionally treated the shader-supplied coordinate as already-normalized `[0, 1)` and multiplied it by the level-0 extent, double-scaling the already-texel-space coordinate an unnormalized-coordinate sampler actually supplies. Fixed by adding a `FEME_SAMPLER_UNNORMALIZED_COORDINATES` flag bit (`RuntimeABI.h`), set from `CreateInfo.unnormalizedCoordinates` in `Sampler::Sampler` (`Image.cpp`), and a new `femeRTUnnormalizeCoord` helper (`FeMeRuntimeCPU.c`) that divides the incoming coordinate by the level-0 extent up front -- before any downstream addressing/filtering math runs -- so every existing computation needs no further changes. Wired into the only 4 sample entry points the Vulkan spec ever permits this bit to reach (`femeCpuImageSample{1D,2D}V4{F32,I32}` -- the spec forbids mipmapping, anisotropy, `compareEnable`, and any Gather/derivative-LOD/array/cube addressing alongside this bit). A first fix attempt (keying new switch cases on the *original* compressed `ResourceFormat` ordinal) was discovered to be dead code: `CommandBuffer.cpp`'s `materializeImageDescriptor` always decodes narrow-channel BC/ETC2/EAC formats into a *widened* uncompressed target format before the descriptor reaches the runtime, so `Img.Format` is never the original narrow format code at border-color-fallback time. Real fix: added a `BorderComponentMask` field to `FemeImageDescriptor` (`RuntimeABI.h`) populated at materialization time (`CommandBuffer.cpp`'s new `compressedFormatBorderComponentMask` helper, computed from the still-available *original* `Img->format()`), threaded through `femeRTExpandBorderColorForFormat`'s new `BorderComponentMaskOverride` parameter (preferred over the `Format`-derived mask whenever nonzero). | ~~L128(b)~~ | **Root-caused `L128(a)` to a specific, precisely-localized bug**, using a new, much faster reproduction vehicle: a hand-minimized `RowCount==5` vertex shader (`attr[0..4]`, well past the `RowCount<=4` real-matrix ceiling but small enough to iterate on in seconds), written directly in MLIR SPIR-V dialect text and exercised through `feme/unittests/Vulkan/DrawTest.cpp`'s own in-process `FeMeVulkanTests` GTest harness (`libfeme_vulkan.so` exercised directly, skipping all `deqp-vk`/CTS-harness overhead) rather than the full CTS/`valgrind` path -- reproduces the crash reliably (~3/3 direct runs, ~3/3 under `gdb`) in seconds instead of minutes; Signature = serializeSignature(Sig);`) **before** calling `runPipeline` -- deliberately, per that function's own comments, to dodge `feme::cpu::EntryWrapperPass`'s loop-/branch-shape paths erasing the original `Function*` (so reading post-pipeline risks a dangling pointer or a renamed function with no attached metadata at all -- confirmed directly: a `Mod.getFunction(WrapperName)` lookup added post-`runPipeline` for this investigation found *zero* `!feme.signature` metadata on the final wrapper function, i.e. metadata is not even propagated across wrapping to make a naive "read later" fix safe). But **the real, authoritative signature-building step for a graphics-pipeline shader is not `runPipeline`'s own internal `CanonicalizeStagePass` call at all** -- it is `feme::vulkan::compileGraphicsStage`'s *separate*, *earlier* `CanonicalizeStagePass().run(...)` call (`GraphicsPipeline.cpp:541`), run *before* `feme::cpu::CompiledStage::create`/`createStage` is ever invoked, specifically so the metadata is already attached by the time `createStage`'s early (pre-`runPipeline`) read captures it. **Root cause, fully confirmed**: no pass anywhere in the pipeline -- neither `compileGraphicsStage`'s early `CanonicalizeStagePass` call nor `runPipeline`'s later, redundant one -- ever unrolls (or otherwise resolves to constant array indices) a compile-time-constant-trip-count loop over an array-typed (`RowCount > 4`) stage-IO global *before* the *first, authoritative* `CanonicalizeStagePass` invocation that actually matters for the exported signature; `L128`'s previously-prototyped forced-unroll pass was placed inside `runPipeline` (Pipeline.cpp), which is *too late* to affect `compileGraphicsStage`'s own earlier, authoritative pass -- explaining why that prototype, even combined with `L128`'s `isDynamicIndexedArrayGlobal` stage-restriction fix, still crashed: it made the *redundant*, ineffective second `CanonicalizeStagePass` call (inside `runPipeline`) succeed, while the *real* one (in `GraphicsPipeline.cpp`, run first, before any unrolling ever happens) still silently produced an incomplete signature. A `RowCount<=4` real matrix never hits this at all, because SPIR-V/glslang always emits its row accesses as separate, already-unrolled loads with no loop for any `CanonicalizeStagePass` invocation to fail to see through -- explaining why this is unique to `RowCount>4` array-shaped vertex/fragment inputs specifically. **Concrete fix for a future session** (not attempted this session -- too large a change, touching a core shared pipeline stage, to land and fully regression-test in the remaining time): move (or duplicate) a loop-unrolling/constant-GEP-recognition pass to run inside `feme::vulkan::compileGraphicsStage`, immediately before its own `CanonicalizeStagePass().run(...)` call at `GraphicsPipeline.cpp:541` -- *not* inside `feme::cpu::runPipeline` -- so the *first, authoritative* signature-building pass sees the already-unrolled, constant-indexed loads. All diagnostic-only scaffolding from this session (the `Pipeline.cpp` forced-unroll prototype, the `FEME_DEBUG_SIG`-gated prints in `StageStorage.cpp`/`CanonicalizeStage.cpp`/`CompiledStage.cpp`, a post-`runPipeline` `Mod.getFunction(WrapperName)` metadata-propagation check) has been reverted (`git checkout --`), leaving no trace in this branch's tracked files except the landed, disabled `DrawTest.L128ARowCount5Repro` (roadmap-referenced fast-repro asset) and this writeup. `ninja check-feme`: 3,276/3,279 Passed, 3 Unsupported, 0 Failed, 0 regressions (only a disabled test and comments added/reverted this session) | L128(a) | **root cause fully confirmed** at the source level (not just disassembly): `feme::vulkan::compileGraphicsStage`'s early, authoritative `CanonicalizeStagePass` call (`GraphicsPipeline.cpp:541`) runs before any loop-unrolling exists anywhere in the pipeline, silently dropping any `RowCount > 4` array-typed stage-IO element from the exported `EntrySignature` even though the compiled shader body still references its `ElementID` directly, producing a null `FemeStageLayout::Elements` pointer at draw time; a fast, disabled, landed repro (`DrawTest.L128ARowCount5Repro`) exists for the next session to validate a fix against; concrete fix location identified (`GraphicsPipeline.cpp:541`, ahead of its own `CanonicalizeStagePass` call) but not attempted -- needs a dedicated session for the pass itself plus full regression testing | P3 |

| L131 | **`pipeline.*.push_constant.*`'s 9 pre-existing, unrelated `pipeline.monolithic.push_constant.*` failures** noted (but explicitly deferred as out-of-scope) by `L129` above, root-caused this session: a Vertex or Fragment entry point with **zero** genuine stage-IO (`in`/`out`) globals -- e.g. a fragment shader that only reads push constants and writes via `imageStore`/a storage resource, never through an ordinary `out` variable (the `overwrite` case), or a shader whose only stage-IO-shaped access is a dynamically- or loop-indexed push-constant-array read that the JIT/SPIR-V-legalization path resolves via an unrelated code path (`dynamic_index_frag`/`vert`, `range_size_128`/`range_size_max`, all 4 with `_command2` variants) -- never entered `CanonicalizeStage.cpp`'s `canonicalizeSPIRVStage`'s signature-building branch (`if (!InputGlobals.empty() || !OutputGlobals.empty())`), so `dxil::setEntrySignature` was never called and no `!feme.signature` metadata was ever attached. `feme::cpu::FragmentWrapperPass::lowerFragmentStageOps` (`FragmentWrapper.cpp`) hard-requires an attached signature once an entry uses *any* stage op (which every fragment entry does unconditionally, via masked-output-store/return-mask calls `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns` always emits for helper-invocation/quad semantics), so the missing metadata surfaced downstream as a JIT symbol-resolution failure (`JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ spirv_var_NN ]`) confirmed via an isolated `FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` trace on `dynamic_index_frag` pre-fix -- **not**, as first speculated while triaging the raw error text, a rejection by `SPIRVPushConstantLowering.cpp`'s `hasOnlyConstantIndices` scope limitation (that limitation remains real and undisturbed, but is not actually exercised by any of these 9 cases; the "dynamic/loop index" theory was a misdiagnosis from surface-level error-message inspection, not a confirmed isolated trace). A prior fix (`H5e-d`/`H91`) had already solved this exact shape for Geometry/Mesh entries (an `else if (Stage == Geometry || Stage == Mesh)` branch attaching an empty signature) but deliberately excluded Vertex/Fragment, reasoning that (unlike Geometry/Mesh, dispatched only through this SPIR-V-only function) a genuine DXIL-origin Vertex/Fragment entry with empty SPIR-V-style globals (always true for DXIL origin) could have its real, already-correct signature clobbered by a blind empty-signature attach -- this ambiguity was the reason a prior rejected fix attempt (`H4g`) failed. Resolved safely this session: confirmed via code inspection that `feme::dxil::MetadataRaisingPass` (`MetadataRaising.cpp`) unconditionally calls `dxil::setEntrySignature` for every DXIL-origin entry point before `CanonicalizeStagePass` ever runs (even for a trivially-empty signature), and `canonicalizeDXILStage` never itself writes signature metadata (only reads it) -- making `!dxil::getEntrySignature(F)` a safe, exact SPIR-V/DXIL origin discriminator (`nullopt` guaranteed for SPIR-V origin, non-`nullopt` guaranteed for DXIL origin). Fixed by extending the `else if` to `Stage == Geometry || Stage == Mesh || ((Stage == Vertex || Stage == Fragment) && !dxil::getEntrySignature(F))`. Fixing this incidentally surfaced two stale, unrelated test assertions that had only ever passed because of this bug's own crash masking a separately-already-relaxed validation, both corrected: `GraphicsPipelineTest.RejectsMissingFragmentOutput` (renamed `AcceptsFragmentWithNoOutputAtAll`, now expecting `VK_SUCCESS`) had its own premise invalidated by the pre-existing, unrelated `H11` fix, which already made "fragment declares no output at a real color-attachment location" spec-legal; `CanonicalizeStageTest.UnresolvableLoadInputIsLeftAlone`'s stale `EXPECT_FALSE(run(*M))` assertion no longer holds now that its exact test shape (no signature, no stage IO) legitimately gets an empty signature attached by this fix. Two new regression tests added, `FragmentWithNoStageIOStillGetsASignature`/`FragmentWithPreAttachedSignatureIsNotClobbered` (the latter standing in for genuine DXIL origin, confirming it is not clobbered), both confirmed via a stash/rebuild round-trip to fail identically to the real bug pre-fix. `ninja check-feme`: 3,276/3,279 Passed, 3 Unsupported, 0 Failed (+2 new tests, 0 regressions -- the 2 stale-test corrections are pre-existing-bug/pre-existing-invariant fixes, not new regressions). New unit test `SIMDizeTest.WidensNarrowingVectorBitCastFromBooleanReduction` (a minimal `fcmp`/`bitcast <4 x i1> to <2 x i2>`/`extractelement` reduction, confirmed via stash/rebuild round-trip to fail identically pre-fix). `ninja check-feme`: 3,290/3,293 Passed, 3 Unsupported, 0 Failed (+1 new test, 0 regressions). eir original IDs (`L7h`/`L7i` sub-letters of `L7`, `L8`, and `L89a`/`L89i`/`L89j`/`L89k` sub-letters of `L89`). They are unchanged in content, dependency and priority, and have been pulled out and renumbered into one consecutive block at the end of the L-series so that the remaining, not-yet-closed HLSL conformance work reads as a single tail rather than being interspersed with closed rows. Every `Depends on` reference elsewhere in this document that pointed at one of the old IDs has been updated to the new one; closed sub-letter siblings under `L7`/`L89` keep their original historical IDs unchanged, since this pass only reorders open work.

Sequencing: L1 already landed; L2-L5 are the highest-value next steps (each
plausibly a single or a handful of root causes affecting many cases, the
same "measure before assigning" discipline G3/J9 already establish), L6 is
now done, M1 is new bookkeeping to re-confirm this section's own historical
measurements used the right driver, and L7 is the largest but
lowest-priority-per-case bucket, deliberately last, since a full per-cluster
scoping survey (mirroring H32's own "H7a closes the first, lowest-risk
cluster" pattern) is needed before it can be split into real, individually
assignable rows.

## Part 2: End-to-end testing roadmap

### 2.1 What exists today

| Layer | Tests |
|---|---|
| CLI translation | `test/Tools/feme/feme-dxil-to-{dxil,spirv,amdgpu}.ll`, `feme-spirv-{null-pipeline,compute-shader,to-amdgpu}.mlir` |
| CLI CPU target | `test/Tools/feme/feme-cpu-{loop,wave-size,accept-bound-resource,reject-unbounded-register-bound}.ll` |
| Execution, hand-written IR | `test/Tools/feme-run/{thread-id-store,multi-group-dispatch,dxil-container-input,reference-mode}.ll` |
| Execution, real HLSL | `test/Tools/feme-run/HLSL/{loop,divergent-control-flow,wave-ops,barrier-groupshared,combined}.hlsl` |
| Differential | `test/Tools/feme-run/differential-harness.test` (5 seeds) |
| Execution, C++ | `unittests/Target/CPU/{JITEngineTest,AOTDispatchTest}.cpp` |

That is real end-to-end coverage — HLSL source through Clang, DXIL import,
raising, the whole CPU pipeline, JIT dispatch, and a `FileCheck`ed numeric
result. The gaps below are about *breadth of axis*, not about the pipeline
being untested.

### 2.2 The axes not yet covered

1. **Wave size** (done by R1). Three of the five executing HLSL end-to-end
   tests whose own computation does not depend on wave width (`loop.hlsl`,
   `divergent-control-flow.hlsl`, `barrier-groupshared.hlsl`) now run at `W`
   in {4, 8, 16, 32} via the `%feme-wave-size-sweep` lit substitution
   (§2.4.1); `wave-ops.hlsl`/`combined.hlsl` genuinely compute a
   wave-size-dependent answer (they use a wave intrinsic directly) and stay
   at `W = 4` until a per-wave-size expected value is worth adding.
2. **The differential harness's own scope** (done for `--divergent`/
   `--loops` by R1; `--unstructured` remains `--reference`-only). Its header
   comment used to say its `--divergent=false --loops=false
   --unstructured=false` restriction existed because milestone 4's widener
   was acyclic/uniform-only, "at which point this harness's scope should
   grow with them". Milestones 6 and 7 landed; the harness did not grow
   until R1, which turns `--divergent`/`--loops` on (the configuration that
   exercises the linearizer and the widened-loop path against ground
   truth) and found the new P0 gap in §1.6's table when `--unstructured`
   was also tried against the normal pipeline (a divergent branch inside a
   loop that should have been diagnosed instead reaching the JIT
   unwidened). `--unstructured` stays `--reference`-only (still real
   coverage: it also caught, and this milestone fixed, a genuine
   `feme-cfg-gen` termination bug in its own irreducible-edge construct)
   until that gap closes.
3. **Front-end equivalence** (done by R10). Both of §1.2's P0 items now
   close: `test/Tools/feme-run/HLSL/front-end-equivalence.hlsl` runs a
   `RWStructuredBuffer<float>` compute shader through both the DXIL and
   SPIR-V front ends and `FileCheck`s the same expected numbers from each.
   The DXIL half is real HLSL compiled by Clang; the SPIR-V half is
   hand-written `spirv` dialect MLIR (see that test's own comment for why
   -- Clang's HLSL front end only reaches SPIR-V through LLVM's in-tree
   SPIRV backend, which this roadmap step's own build did not configure),
   so it is not literally *one* `.hlsl` source compiled twice, but the same
   shader's logic independently authored for each front end and checked
   for agreement, which is the property this item exists to give SPIR-V
   input the same confidence the DXIL side already has.
4. **JIT vs AOT** (done by R8). `AOTDispatchTest.cpp` establishes the pattern
   in `gtest` for one shader; `feme-run --object` now loads a shader
   compiled with `feme --target=<host>` -- a real object file -- with
   `orc::LLJIT::addObjectFile` and dispatches it directly, so `lit` covers
   the same AOT path (see test/Tools/feme-run/feme-run-object-aot.ll).
5. **Optimization level** (done by R14). Every end-to-end HLSL execution
   test JITs its shader through `feme::cpu::JITEngine`'s `OptimizerPipeline`
   pass, which has always run at a hardcoded `CodeGenOptLevel::Default`
   (`-O2`-equivalent, see `JITEngine.cpp`'s `toOptimizationLevel`) with no
   way for a test to pick a different level, so nothing ever checked that a
   shader's answer stays the same across levels. `feme-run` gains a `-O`
   flag (matching `llc`'s own spelling, `cl::Prefix` and all) that feeds
   `JITOptions::OptLevel` -- a field that already existed for this purpose
   but was never wired to the CLI; `test/Tools/feme-run/HLSL/opt-level-
   differential.hlsl` runs the same shader (a small unrolled per-lane
   multiply-add loop, with real reassociation/vectorization opportunities
   for the optimizer to find) at `-O0` through `-O3` and checks all four
   produce identical output. This is a different knob from `feme`'s own
   `-O0`/.../`-Od` (`feme::FrontendOptions`, which select the level the
   *front-end* pipeline runs its optimizer at, before any CPU-specific
   lowering) -- the two are independent, and this item is specifically
   about the JIT path's own post-CPU-lowering optimization pass.
6. **Round trips** (DXIL→DXIL→run done by R14; SPIR-V→SPIR-V→run remains
   blocked, see below). `feme-dxil-to-dxil.ll` checks a DXIL→DXIL retarget
   produces a container, but no test re-imports the produced artifact and
   executes it. `test/Tools/feme-run/HLSL/dxil-roundtrip-execute.hlsl`
   closes this: real HLSL compiled to a DXContainer, retargeted back to
   `dxil` through the full `feme` CLI (a second pass through
   `feme::DXILImporter`/the raising passes/`feme::DXILExporter`), and the
   *result* of that round trip executed and `FileCheck`ed through
   `feme-run` -- a much stronger statement than one that only parses the
   output. The equivalent SPIR-V→SPIR-V→run test turns out not to be
   possible yet: `feme --target=spirv` on a SPIR-V-derived module retargets
   through `feme::SPIRVExporter`, which (unlike the hand-authored `spirv`
   dialect fixtures every existing SPIR-V test in this tree assembles with
   `feme-translate --serialize-spirv`) emits its binary through LLVM's own
   in-tree SPIR-V code generator (`feme::TargetMachineBackend`) -- and
   `feme::SPIRVImporter` (a thin wrapper around MLIR's `spirv::deserialize`,
   see Design.md's SPIR-V section) cannot parse that generator's own
   output back in (`error: unhandled opcode 83` -- `OpAccessChain` --
   deserializing a module that `feme-run` executes just fine *before* that
   round trip). This is a genuine incompatibility between two independently
   evolving upstream SPIR-V producers/consumers (LLVM's SPIR-V backend and
   MLIR's SPIR-V deserializer); this roadmap step's own scope was testing,
   not new import breadth, so fixing the deserializer itself was left for a
   dedicated step -- see the "Known gap" this adds to Design.md's SPIR-V
   section for the concrete repro, and roadmap R38, which now tracks
   closing it directly (both live in this same tree).
7. **Resource shapes** (typed buffers done by R8). Every executing test
   used to use an unstructured raw buffer, because that was all
   `feme-run`'s heap YAML could describe (§1.6); it now also accepts
   `kind`/`format`/`stride`, and `typed-buffer.hlsl` exercises a real
   `RWBuffer<float4>`. Structured-buffer strides and constant buffers
   remain untested by execution (the heap YAML can describe them, but no
   test yet does).
8. **DXBC.** CLI-level (`feme`/`feme-translate`) end-to-end coverage now
   exists, per §1.4's R7 entry (`test/Tools/feme/feme-dxbc-to-dxil.dxasm`).
   Execution (a DXBC-derived module reaching `feme-run`/the CPU target) is
   still uncovered -- `feme-run` only accepts `.ll`/`.bc`/DXIL, per §1.2.

### 2.3 The interesting cases to add

Concretely, in rough value order, all under `test/Tools/feme-run/HLSL/`
unless noted:

- **`reduction.hlsl`** (done by R5) — a barrier inside a loop, folding
  per-lane contributions with `WaveActiveSum` and publishing the result
  through groupshared. Directly exercises §1.6's "barrier inside a loop is
  diagnosed" narrowing (now closed for this uniform-loop shape); an honest
  groupshared *tree* reduction (indexing `groupshared` by
  `SV_GroupThreadID`) was blocked on §1.6's separate "Divergent
  groupshared access is diagnosed" row, which R5 found is one case broader
  than recorded (a *masked* store at a uniform address, not just a
  divergent index) -- both are now closed by R23.
- **`prefix-sum.hlsl`** (done by R4) — `WavePrefixSum`/`WavePrefixCountBits`
  over a divergent mask; exercises §1.3's flag-selected `WavePrefixOp`
  family.
- **`histogram.hlsl`** — divergent atomics into a shared buffer. This is the
  scalarization fallback's only realistic workload, and the one that catches
  §1.6's unmasked-lane P0 (done: a single groupshared counter a divergent
  condition gates `InterlockedAdd` into, reading the atomic's own return
  value rather than a separate reload -- a genuine multi-bucket histogram,
  indexing a groupshared array by a divergent bucket, was blocked on
  §1.6's separate "Divergent groupshared access is diagnosed" row (closed
  by R23): Clang itself folds an `if`/`else` each doing the same op on a
  different constant address into a single `select`-of-pointer
  `atomicrmw`, the address-divergent shape that narrowing covered).
- **`ballot.hlsl`** (done by R3) — `WaveActiveBallot` + `countbits`; was
  gated on §1.3's aggregate-returning mechanism.
- **`nested-divergence.hlsl`** — divergent loop containing a divergent
  diamond containing an early return. The linearizer's hardest supported
  shape, currently only reached through generated CFGs.
- **`multi-group-barrier.hlsl`** (done by R5) — several groups, each
  publishing through two barrier-separated groupshared slots, asserting
  groups do not observe each other's memory.
- **`matrix-multiply.hlsl`** — tiled, groupshared-staged, loop-heavy; the
  closest thing to a real workload, and a natural first performance
  regression fixture for milestone 12/13.
- **`typed-buffer.hlsl`** (done by R8) — `RWBuffer<float4>` with a real
  format (`r32g32b32a32_float`), using §2.4's heap YAML work.
- **A DXBC pair** under `test/Tools/feme/`: a `dxbc-as`-assembled `.dxasm`
  fixture retargeted with `feme --target=dxil`, and the same fixture executed
  through `feme-run` once DXBC import reaches `Driver` (§1.4).

Each of these is written the way the existing HLSL tests are — `split-file`,
`clang -target dxil--shadermodel6.5-compute`, a `heap.yaml`, a `CHECK` line
of numbers — so the incremental cost per shader is small once the
prerequisites in §2.4 exist.

### 2.4 Test infrastructure prerequisites

These are the changes that make §2.3 cheap rather than repetitive, and each
is small enough to land on its own:

1. **A wave-size sweep substitution** (done by R1: `%feme-wave-size-sweep`,
   feme/utils/feme-wave-size-sweep.py). A lit substitution that runs one
   input at several wave sizes and `FileCheck`s each run's output, so a
   shader opts into the sweep by one substitution instead of four `RUN:`
   lines.
2. **`feme-run` SPIR-V input** (done by R10). `feme-run` now links
   `FeMeImportSPIRV`/`FeMeTranslateSPIRV` alongside `FeMeImportDXIL`, and
   `loadModule` sniffs a SPIR-V binary's own magic number the same way
   `feme::Driver::detectFormat` does, rather than re-deriving that logic
   (the DXIL/SPIR-V import + translation split is small enough that
   sharing `Driver`'s exact detection code was not worth the coupling; see
   `feme-run`'s own file comment). Unlocks §2.2's front-end-equivalence
   axis, once the CPU pipeline itself could also execute a SPIR-V-sourced
   module's resource access and builtin-variable idiom (see
   `feme::cpu::SPIRVResourceLoweringPass`/`SPIRVBuiltinFoldingPass` and
   the Deviation note roadmap step R10 adds to
   feme/docs/FeMeCPUDesign.md's Status section).
3. **Heap YAML `kind`/`format`/`stride`** (done by R8). FeMeCPUDesign.md
   already specified the richer schema; milestone 11 shipped the raw-buffer
   subset. `feme-run`'s `resource-heap`/`bindings` entries now accept all
   three, unlocking §2.3's typed-buffer cases and stopping tests from
   hand-encoding float bit patterns as integers.
4. **A `%feme-run-differential` harness helper** (done by R1:
   feme/utils/feme-run-differential.py). Takes a seed list, a `feme-cfg-gen`
   flag set, and a wave-size list, generating each seed once and diffing its
   `--reference` output against every requested wave size -- replacing the
   differential harness's previous five copy-pasted five-line blocks with
   one substitution per shape/wave-size combination, so §2.2's item 2 can
   grow the shape space without growing the file. It also refuses to trust
   a `feme-run` invocation that printed a diagnostic even if its exit code
   was zero (see §1.6's new divergent-branch-in-a-loop gap, found by this
   helper), so a shape is only accepted once the pipeline ran it with no
   caveats.
5. **An AOT lit recipe** (done by R8). `feme-run --object` loads a shader
   compiled with `feme --target=<host-triple>` -- a real object file -- with
   `orc::LLJIT::addObjectFile` and dispatches it directly through
   `feme::cpu::runDispatch`, so AOT is covered by `lit`, not only by
   `gtest` (test/Tools/feme-run/feme-run-object-aot.ll).
6. **`check-feme-fuzz` (done by R6).** Per §1.7: bounded (`-runs=N`,
   seed-corpus-only) runs of every fuzz target, wired as a dependency of
   nothing by default (`ninja check-feme-fuzz` runs it explicitly) but with
   every fuzz target added to `FEME_TEST_DEPENDS` so `ninja check-feme`
   still builds all of them.

### 2.5 Corpus discipline

Two rules the existing tests already follow, worth stating so the additions
keep following them:

- **No binary fixtures.** Every input is assembled at test time — `.hlsl`
  through `clang`, `.ll` through `llvm-as`/`llc`, `.yaml` through
  `yaml2obj`, `.dxasm` through `dxbc-as` (Design.md, "Avoiding binary test
  fixtures").
- **Every restructurization bug found anywhere reduces into a named shape
  file** under `test/Transforms/CPU/CFG/` (FeMeCPUDesign.md, "CFG
  restructurization test suite", layer 1).

### 2.6 Testing the graphics and API runtime track

§2.1–§2.5 are about the compute track's breadth. The new components need
their own layers, and three of them are infrastructure that must exist before
the first shader-facing milestone rather than alongside it.

#### 2.6.1 Infrastructure prerequisites

1. **An image resource class in `feme-run`'s heap YAML.** Today's schema
   accepts `resource-heap`/`bindings` entries with `kind`/`format`/`stride`
   (§2.4.3). An image entry additionally needs dimensionality, extent, mip and
   array ranges, format, and layout. Required by every G2 test and by the
   textual image fixtures G3 onward compare against.
2. **`feme-render`.** A new tool that renders a textual scene description to a
   textual image fixture through the graphics executor, the way `feme-run`
   dispatches a compute shader. It is specified in Design.md's "Testing
   Tools" and has a [CommandGuide page](CommandGuide/feme-render.md);
   only the implementation is left. Needed from G3; the alternative — growing
   `feme-run` a draw mode — mixes two very different argument models.
3. **Textual scene and image fixtures.** §2.5's "no binary fixtures" rule
   applies unchanged: scenes, textures and expected images are text, generated
   or compared at test time. This is what makes edge-rule failures reviewable
   in a diff. Both formats are specified in Design.md's "Textual scene and
   image fixtures": one image format serves as texture input, expected output
   and actual-output dump, compared exactly by default, and a scene is YAML
   extending `feme-run`'s heap schema with attachments, pipeline state and
   vertex streams spelled in FeMe's own enumerations rather than any API's.

Two more become prerequisites once the runtimes start:

4. **Lit clients under `test/Vulkan/`** running against the build-tree
   manifest via `VK_DRIVER_FILES`, plus a second-ICD coexistence
   configuration and an exported-dynamic-symbol check against the version
   script (§1.9).
5. **A differential reference for each API.** Vulkan compares against Mesa's
   lavapipe, Direct3D against Microsoft's WARP, in both cases only for the
   subset each milestone actually advertises. Both are optional, detected
   dependencies: a missing reference must skip, never fail.

#### 2.6.2 Layers

The graphics design's six layers map onto this tree as:

| Layer | Where | First needed |
|---|---|---|
| Core import convergence (same canonical signature/operations from DXIL and SPIR-V) | `test/Transforms/Graphics/` | G0 |
| CPU pass tests at wave sizes 4, 8 and one native width, checking mask, quad, barrier, output-bound and spill invariants | `test/Transforms/CPU/Graphics/` | G1 |
| Runtime helper tests exhausting image coordinates, formats, filtering, robustness and helper-lane side effects | `unittests/Graphics/` | G2 |
| Fixed-function unit tests with no shader frontend (clipping, edge rules, interpolation, depth/stencil, blend, tessellator, meshlet validation, BVH build/traversal, layout math) | `unittests/Graphics/`, `unittests/RayTracing/` | G3 |
| End-to-end executor tests rendering textual scenes | `test/Tools/feme-render/` | G3 |
| Frontend tests creating real Vulkan/Direct3D pipelines | `test/Vulkan/`, `test/Direct3D/` | V1, W1 |

#### 2.6.3 Metamorphic properties

These are the checks that catch the failures image comparison alone does not,
and each should land with the milestone that makes it meaningful rather than
as a late sweep:

- identical wave-size-independent output across wave sizes (extends §2.2.1's
  existing sweep to stages);
- identical deterministic output across worker counts and tile traversal
  orders — the graphics counterpart of §2.2's differential harness, and the
  first thing a thread-pooled dispatch (§1.6) needs;
- identical linked varyings after irrelevant signature elements are added;
- identical sampling through storage-compatible API format aliases;
- no resource or attachment change from helper-only quads;
- the same canonical behavior from equivalent DXIL and SPIR-V inputs — the
  stage-shaped version of §2.2.3's front-end equivalence test;
- identical primitive streams from equivalent conventional and mesh pipelines;
- identical hits between BVH traversal and brute-force intersection;
- identical scalar and packetized ray continuation results.

#### 2.6.4 Fuzzing and sanitizers

§1.7's rule — "a fuzzing harness lands alongside each importer" — generalizes
to "alongside each attacker-controlled parser". The new ones are descriptor
updates, pipeline-cache blobs, command-stream decoding, serialized root
signatures, artifact/`StageArtifactInfo` blobs, and acceleration-structure
builds. Each belongs in `check-feme-fuzz` (§2.4.6) with its own seed corpus
the day its parser lands.

Sanitizer configurations stop being §1.7's P1 nice-to-have: ASan/UBSan for
import and raster code, TSan for prepared-draw and tile scheduling (and for
queue/pipeline concurrency in both runtimes), forced allocation/JIT failure
injection, and stress configurations that cap tessellation, mesh queues,
continuation memory and ray recursion at small values so every
resource-exhaustion path is exercised.

## Part 3: Suggested sequencing

Each step is independently landable and independently testable; the
dependency column is the only ordering constraint.

§3.1's table is the compute and retargeting track (R1–R15, the original
sequencing). §3.2 adds the graphics core and CPU stage work (R16–R37), and
§3.3 places the two API runtimes' own milestones against it. R16 onward may
proceed in parallel with R15, which has no dependents.

### 3.1 Compute and retargeting track

R1 comes first deliberately, and for the same reason FeMeCPUDesign.md put its
own restructurization suite before its linearizer: it is the step that makes
every subsequent step's failures visible as a diff instead of as a wrong
number in a `CHECK` line nobody wrote yet.

### 3.2 Graphics core and CPU stage track

Every step here lands in `feme` proper — core reflection, the CPU target, and
the two new executor libraries — and is testable through `feme-opt`,
`feme-run`, `feme-render` and `gtest` without any API runtime existing. The
"Milestone" column is the FeMeGraphicsDesign.md milestone the step belongs to;
a milestone is complete when its own completion test passes, which is normally
the last step carrying its name.
